title: From The Sunday Read Archives: ‘My Mustache, My Self’

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 Dealbook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: I'm Wesley Morris.
sentences.zh: 我是韦斯利·莫里斯。

sentences.en: I am a critic at the New York Times, and I wrote an essay about my mustache.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的一名评论员，我写了一篇关于我胡子的文章。

sentences.en: I grew this thing the way a lot of people did a lot of things for the first time, or, you know, out of boredom or curiosity during this pandemic,
sentences.zh: 我留起这玩意儿的方式，就像很多人第一次做很多事情一样，或者说，你知道，是在疫情期间出于无聊或好奇，

sentences.en: to stave off the misery outside our windows and front doors.
sentences.zh: 为了抵御窗外和门外的那种苦闷。

sentences.en: I decided with my friend Brian to grow a mustache.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友布莱恩决定一起留胡子。

sentences.en: And so we get on the phone one day, we do a Zoom call, and he reveals his, and it's not good.
sentences.zh: 有一天我们通了电话，开了个视频会议，他展示了他的胡子，结果并不好看。

sentences.en: By his own admission, it is a handlebar mustache, not his thing.
sentences.zh: 据他自己承认，那是种八字胡，不适合他。

sentences.en: And mine is a little more traditional.
sentences.zh: 而我的则更传统一些。

sentences.en: It is a short, sharp thing that we both agreed looked pretty good.
sentences.zh: 那是一撮短小、利落的胡子，我们俩都觉得看起来还不错。

sentences.en: And he got rid of his, I decided to keep mine, and it felt to me like the most right thing I had done with my face in my entire adult life.
sentences.zh: 后来他把胡子刮了，我决定留着，我觉得这是我成年以来在脸上做过的最正确的事情。

sentences.en: I don't really know why I kept it, except it was speaking to me, and I was trying to hear what it was saying.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道为什么我留着它，只是它好像在跟我说话，而我正试图听清它在说什么。

sentences.en: And one day, I was on a different call with a different friend, my friend Nikita, and she kind of put the whole thing in perspective for me, and it cracked my life open.
sentences.zh: 有一天，我和另一个朋友尼基塔通电话，她的一番话让我对整件事有了新的认识，也彻底打开了我的心扉。

sentences.en: I don't think I'm going to be the same person after that, and it is entirely connected to what this thing on my face makes me feel and connects me to.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在那之后我不再是同一个人了，这完全与我脸上这东西带给我的感受以及它与我的联系有关。

sentences.en: In many ways, I want to thank Brian for making us go on this dare, and I want to thank my friend Nikita for saying what she said to make me think about my whole life.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，我要感谢布莱恩让我们接受了这个挑战，也要感谢我的朋友尼基塔，她的话让我开始思考我的一生。

sentences.en: I'm getting a little emotional just thinking about that.
sentences.zh: 想到这些，我甚至有点激动。

sentences.en: But yeah, I wanted to try to write it through, and what you're about to hear is the result.
sentences.zh: 但没错，我想试着把它写出来，你接下来听到的就是结果。

sentences.en: Here is my essay, My Mustache, read by Dion Graham.
sentences.zh: 这是我的文章《我的胡子》，由迪翁·格雷厄姆朗读。

sentences.en: Like a lot of men, in pursuit of novelty and amusement during these months of isolation, I grew a mustache.
sentences.zh: 像许多男人一样，为了在这些隔离的日子里寻求新鲜感和乐趣，我留了胡子。

sentences.en: The reviews were predictably mixed and predictably predictable.
sentences.zh: 评价不出所料地褒贬不一，且不出所料地在意料之中。

sentences.en: Porny?
sentences.zh: 像色情片里的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Creepy?
sentences.zh: 令人毛骨悚然？

sentences.en: Obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然。
70年代风格？

sentences.en: True.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The 18 and 1970s.
sentences.zh: 18世纪和1970年代的风格。

sentences.en: On some video calls, I heard rugged and extra gay.
sentences.zh: 在一些视频通话中，我听到有人说它看起来很粗犷，而且特别“基”。

sentences.en: Someone I love called me zaddy.
sentences.zh: 我爱的一个人叫我“辣爹”。

sentences.en: Children were harsh.
sentences.zh: 孩子们则很刻薄。

sentences.en: My 11-year-old nephew told his Minecraft friends that his uncle has this mustache.
sentences.zh: 我11岁的侄子告诉他的《我的世界》游戏好友，他叔叔留了这种胡子。

sentences.en: The mid-game disgust was audible through his headset.
sentences.zh: 通过他的耳机，能清晰地听到游戏进行到一半时传来的厌恶声。

sentences.en: In August, I spent two weeks with my niece, who's seven.
sentences.zh: 八月份，我和七岁的侄女待了两周。

sentences.en: She would rise each morning, dismayed anew, to be spending another day looking at the hair on my face.
sentences.zh: 她每天早上起床时，看到我脸上的胡子，都会再次感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Once, she climbed on my back and began combing the mustache with her fingers, whispering in the warmest tones of endearment,
sentences.zh: 有一次，她爬到我背上，开始用手指梳理我的胡子，用最亲昵的语气低声说：

sentences.en: Uncle Wesley, when are you going to shave this thing off?
sentences.zh: “韦斯利叔叔，你什么时候把这东西刮掉？”

sentences.en: It hasn't been all bad.
sentences.zh: 情况也不全是那么糟糕。

sentences.en: Halfway through a quick stop and chat outside a friend's house in July, he and I removed our masks and exploded at the sight of each other.
sentences.zh: 七月的一天，我在朋友家门外短暂停留聊天，聊到一半时，我们摘下口罩，看到对方的样子都笑喷了。

sentences.en: No way!
sentences.zh: 不会吧！

sentences.en: Mustache!
sentences.zh: 胡子！

sentences.en: I spent video meetings searching amid the boxes for other mustaches, to admire the way they enhance eyes and redefine faces with a force of irreversible handsomeness.
sentences.zh: 我在视频会议中会在屏幕方框里搜寻其他人的胡子，欣赏它们如何衬托双眼，并以一种不可逆转的帅气感重塑面部轮廓。

sentences.en: The way Burt Reynolds never made the same kind of sense without his.
sentences.zh: 就像伯特·雷诺兹如果没有胡子，就再也没有那种感觉了一样。

sentences.en: The mustache aged me.
sentences.zh: 胡子让我显老了。

sentences.en: People didn't mind letting me know that, either.
sentences.zh: 人们也不介意让我知道这一点。

sentences.en: But so what?
sentences.zh: 但那又怎样？

sentences.en: It pulled me past mature to a particular kind of distinguished.
sentences.zh: 它让我超越了成熟，达到了一种独特的风度。

sentences.en: It looks fetching, for instance, with suits I currently have no logical reason to wear.
sentences.zh: 例如，它搭配那些我目前没有理由穿的西装，看起来很迷人。

sentences.en: One afternoon, on a group call to celebrate a friend's good news, somebody said what I didn't know I needed to hear.
sentences.zh: 一天下午，在庆祝朋友好消息的群组通话中，有人说了一句我没意识到自己需要听到的话。

sentences.en: More reviews were pouring in, thumbs down mostly, but I was already committed at that point.
sentences.zh: 更多的评价纷至沓来，大多是差评，但那时我已经投入其中了。

sentences.en: I just didn't know to what.
sentences.zh: 只是我不知道投入到了什么之中。

sentences.en: That's when my friend chimed in, you look like a lawyer for the NAACP Legal Defense Fund.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我的朋友插话道：“你看起来像全国有色人种协进会法律辩护基金会的律师。”

sentences.en: What I remember was laughter.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时大家都笑了。

sentences.en: But where someone might have sensed shade being thrown, I experienced the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但当别人可能觉得这是在讽刺时，我却感受到了相反的意味。

sentences.en: A light had been shown.
sentences.zh: 一盏灯被点亮了。

sentences.en: It was said as a winking correction and an earnest clarification.
sentences.zh: 这话既像是一种调侃的纠正，又像是一种真诚的阐释。

sentences.en: Y'all, this is what it is.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，这就是它的意义所在。

sentences.en: The call moved on, but I didn't.
sentences.zh: 通话继续进行，但我却停留在那里。

sentences.en: That is what it is.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的意义。

sentences.en: One of the sweetest, truest things anybody had said about me in a long time.
sentences.zh: 这是很久以来别人对我说过的最甜蜜、最真实的话之一。

sentences.en: My friend had identified a mighty American tradition and placed my face within it.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友识别出了一种伟大的美国传统，并将我的脸置于其中。

sentences.en: Anytime 20th century black people found themselves entangled in racialized peril, anytime the roots of racism pushed up some new, hideous weed,
sentences.zh: 每当20世纪的黑人发现自己陷入种族主义的危险之中，每当种族主义的根系长出某种新的、丑陋的杂草时，

sentences.en: a thoughtful-looking, solemn-seeming, crisply-attired gentleman would be photographed entering a
sentences.zh: 总会有一位看起来深思熟虑、神情庄重、衣着干练的绅士被拍到走进

sentences.en: courthouse or seated somewhere, a library, a living room, alongside the wronged and imperiled.
sentences.zh: 法院，或者坐在某个地方——图书馆、客厅里，与那些受冤屈和处于危险中的人在一起。

sentences.en: He was probably a lawyer, and he was likely to have been mustached.
sentences.zh: 他很可能是一位律师，而且很可能留着胡子。

sentences.en: Thurgood Marshall started the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People's Legal Defense and Education Fund 80 years ago.
sentences.zh: 瑟古德·马歇尔在80年前创立了全国有色人种协进会法律辩护与教育基金会。

sentences.en: It still exists.
sentences.zh: 它至今仍然存在。

sentences.en: Sherilyn Ifill is in charge.
sentences.zh: 谢丽琳·伊菲尔负责管理它。

sentences.en: The LDF's most famous cases include Shelley v.
sentences.zh: 法律辩护基金会最著名的案件包括雪莉诉

sentences.en: Kramer, which, in effect, forbade landlords from refusing to rent to black people, and Brown v.
sentences.zh: 克莱默案，该案实际上禁止了房东拒绝向黑人出租房屋，以及布朗诉

sentences.en: Board of Education, the crown jewel in the fund's many school desegregation challenges.
sentences.zh: 教育委员会案，这是该基金会众多学校废除种族隔离挑战中的皇冠明珠。

sentences.en: Marshall was, essentially, the civil rights movement's legal strategiSt.
sentences.zh: 马歇尔本质上是民权运动的法律战略家。

sentences.en: And in case after case, he arrived at the Supreme Court in elegant tailoring and sharp haircuts.
sentences.zh: 在一次又一次的案件中，他总是穿着优雅的西装，留着利落的发型，出现在最高法院。

sentences.en: A decade later, Marshall was on the court.
sentences.zh: 十年后，马歇尔进入了最高法院。

sentences.en: And any time he donned that robe and those horn-rimmed spectacles, every time he shined at oral arguments, he did so wearing a mustache.
sentences.zh: 每当他穿上法袍，戴上那副玳瑁眼镜，每当他在口头辩论中大放异彩时，他都留着胡子。

sentences.en: The glasses and jowls emphasized his famous air of wisdom.
sentences.zh: 眼镜和下垂的脸颊突显了他那著名的智慧气质。

sentences.en: The mustache bestowed a grounding flourish.
sentences.zh: 胡子则赋予了他一种沉稳的修饰。

sentences.en: In 1954, when the court ruled in Brown, it wasn't so rare to see a mustached man.
sentences.zh: 1954年，当最高法院对布朗案作出裁决时，看到留胡子的男人并不罕见。

sentences.en: They were a common feature among blue-collar Joes.
sentences.zh: 那是蓝领阶层中常见的特征。

sentences.en: Charlie Chaplin and Errol Flynn had been stars, and the country hadn't quite finished with Clark Gable.
sentences.zh: 查理·卓别林和埃罗尔·弗林曾是巨星，而美国对克拉克·盖博的热度也还没完全消退。

sentences.en: Ernest Hemingway had aligned the mustache with distinctly American ideas of masculine bravado, concision, and sport.
sentences.zh: 欧内斯特·海明威将胡子与美国独特的男性勇敢、简洁和运动理念联系在了一起。

sentences.en: But a mustache could also be a softener, a grace note.
sentences.zh: 但胡子也可以是一种柔化剂，一种优雅的点缀。

sentences.en: A mustache advertised a certain commitment to civility.
sentences.zh: 胡子宣扬了一种对文明的某种承诺。

sentences.en: On a man like Gable, it embellished his rough edges, gave his character's chauvinism a classy place to land.
sentences.zh: 在像盖博这样的男人脸上，它修饰了他粗犷的棱角，让他角色的沙文主义有了一个体面的落脚点。

sentences.en: On black men, a mustache told a different story.
sentences.zh: 而在黑人男性的脸上，胡子讲述了另一个故事。

sentences.en: It was fashionable, but it was more than that.
sentences.zh: 它很时髦，但不仅于此。

sentences.en: On a black man, it signified values, perseverance, seriousness, rigor.
sentences.zh: 在黑人男性脸上，它象征着价值观、毅力、严肃和严谨。

sentences.en: It should be noted that the superstar ideological iconoclast, among the freedom fighters, Malcolm X, did battle accordingly.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，在自由战士中，那位超级意识形态偶像破坏者马尔科姆·X，也相应地进行了抗争。

sentences.en: He was the only prominent American leader of any race with a goatee.
sentences.zh: 他是唯一一位留着山羊胡的著名美国领袖，无论种族如何。

sentences.en: In the days after that congratulations video call, the euphoria of having been tagged as part of some illustrious legacy tapered off.
sentences.zh: 在那次祝贺视频通话后的几天里，那种被贴上某种辉煌遗产一部分标签的欣快感逐渐消退了。

sentences.en: The mustache had certainly conjoined me to a past I was flattered to be associated with, however superficially, but there were implications.
sentences.zh: 胡子确实将我与一段我为之感到荣幸的过去联系在了一起，尽管只是表面上的，但其中还有更深层的含义。

sentences.en: During the later stages of the movement, a mustached man opened himself up to charges of white appeasement and Uncle Tom-ism.
sentences.zh: 在运动的后期，留胡子的男人容易受到“讨好白人”和“汤姆叔叔”式的指责。

sentences.en: Not because of the mustache, obviously, but because of the approach of the sort of person who would choose to wear one.
sentences.zh: 显然不是因为胡子本身，而是因为那种会选择留胡子的人所采取的立场。

sentences.en: Such a person might not have been considered radical enough, down enough, black enough.
sentences.zh: 这样的人可能不会被认为足够激进、足够坚定、足够“黑”。

sentences.en: The civil rights mustache was strategically tolerant.
sentences.zh: 民权运动时期的胡子在策略上是宽容的。

sentences.en: It didn't advocate burning anything down.
sentences.zh: 它不主张烧毁任何东西。

sentences.en: It ran for office, and sometimes it won.
sentences.zh: 它竞选公职，有时还会获胜。

sentences.en: It was establishmentarian, compromising, and eventually, come the infernos at the close of the 1960s, it fell out of fashion,
sentences.zh: 它是建制派的，是妥协的，最终，随着1960年代末的烈火燃起，它不再流行，

sentences.en: in part because it fell out of step with the urgency of the moment.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是它跟不上当时紧迫的形势。

sentences.en: The black mustache didn't end with the disillusionments of the post-civil rights era.
sentences.zh: 黑人的胡子并没有随着民权运动后时代的幻灭而终结。

sentences.en: Jim Brown, Stevie Wonder, Richard Roundtree,
sentences.zh: 吉姆·布朗、史蒂夫·旺达、理查德·朗特里、

sentences.en: Billy D.
sentences.zh: 比利·迪·

sentences.en: Williams, Lionel Richie,
sentences.zh: 威廉姆斯、莱昂纳尔·里奇、

sentences.en: Sherman Hemsley, Carl Weathers,
sentences.zh: 谢尔曼·汉姆斯利、卡尔·韦瑟斯、

sentences.en: James Brown, Arsenio Hall, and Eddie Murphy wore one.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·布朗、阿塞尼奥·霍尔和埃迪·墨菲都留过胡子。

sentences.en: It's just that no higher calling officially united them.
sentences.zh: 只是再也没有更高的使命将他们正式团结在一起了。

sentences.en: Their mustaches were freelance signatures, the mark of an individual rather than a people's emblem.
sentences.zh: 他们的胡子是个人的自由签名，是个体的标志，而不是一个民族的象征。

sentences.en: At some point in the 1970s, and through at least 1980,
sentences.zh: 在1970年代的某个时候，至少到1980年，

sentences.en: Muhammad Ali grew one you could attach to a broom handle.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里留了一撮你可以把它系在扫帚柄上的胡子。

sentences.en: Donnie Simpson hosted BET's Video Soul with a tapered number and a silky smoothness that could line a tuxedo jacket.
sentences.zh: 唐尼·辛普森主持 BET 的《Video Soul》节目时，留着修剪整齐的胡子，那种丝滑感足以衬托一件燕尾服外套。

sentences.en: Through a rock in an old Jet magazine from the 1980s, you'll hit somebody's mustache.
sentences.zh: 翻开一本1980年代的旧《Jet》杂志，你总会看到某人的胡子。

sentences.en: But well before then, the politics of self-presentation had coalesced around grander, less deniable hair.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前很久，自我展示的政治已经围绕着更宏大、更不可否认的头发凝聚起来了。

sentences.en: They migrated to the Afro.
sentences.zh: 它们转向了爆炸头。

sentences.en: A mustache might have been a dignified symbol in the pursuit of equality, but there was nothing inherently black about it.
sentences.zh: 胡子可能是追求平等的尊严象征，但它本身并没有什么本质上的“黑人”属性。

sentences.en: A mustache meant business.
sentences.zh: 胡子意味着干正事。

sentences.en: An afro meant power.
sentences.zh: 爆炸头意味着力量。

sentences.en: I knew before the summer's Black Lives Matter protests that my mustache made me look like a bougie race man.
sentences.zh: 在今年夏天的“黑人的命也是命”抗议活动之前，我就知道我的胡子让我看起来像个资产阶级式的“种族斗士”。

sentences.en: A professional, seemingly humorless, middle-class Negro.
sentences.zh: 一个专业的、看似毫无幽默感的中产阶级黑人。

sentences.en: A moderate who believes that presentation is a crucial component of the advancement part of the NAACP mission.
sentences.zh: 一个温和派，相信形象是全国有色人种协进会使命中“进步”部分的关键组成部分。

sentences.en: Someone who doesn't mind a little respectability because he believes his people deserve respect.
sentences.zh: 一个不介意讲究体面的人，因为他相信他的人民理应得到尊重。

sentences.en: It's a look to ponder as the country finds itself churning once again over ceaseless questions of advancement and justice and the right to be left to hell alone.
sentences.zh: 当这个国家再次因关于进步、正义以及“被独自留下来”的权利等无休止的问题而动荡不安时，这是一个值得深思的形象。

sentences.en: I live a street over from a thoroughfare where the protests happened almost nightly in June and July.
sentences.zh: 我住的地方离一条主干道只有一个街区，六月和七月几乎每晚都有抗议活动发生。

sentences.en: I could hear their approach from my living room.
sentences.zh: 在客厅里我就能听到他们走近的声音。

sentences.en: One evening, I stood at a corner, moved, as thousands of people passed.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，我站在街角，看着成千上万的人走过，深受触动。

sentences.en: Friends, colleagues, co-workers, some guy I went on a blind date with a million years ago, chanting, brandishing banners and buttons.
sentences.zh: 朋友、同事、共事者，还有我一万年前约会过的一个人，他们高喊着口号，挥舞着横幅和徽章。

sentences.en: Some protesters had their fists raised in a Black Power salute.
sentences.zh: 一些抗议者举起拳头，行“黑人权力”礼。

sentences.en: So I raised mine.
sentences.zh: 于是我也举起了我的拳头。

sentences.en: Not a gesture I would normally make.
sentences.zh: 这不是我通常会做的动作。

sentences.en: But there was something about seeing so many white people lifting their arms that goaded me into doing it, too.
sentences.zh: 但看到那么多白人举起手臂，某种东西促使我也跟着做了。

sentences.en: Mine kept lowering itself, so I had to jerk it to its fullest, most committed extension.
sentences.zh: 我的手臂总是往下掉，所以我不得不猛地把它伸到最极限、最坚定的位置。

sentences.en: I felt out of control.
sentences.zh: 我感到无法控制自己。

sentences.en: Like Edward Norton throwing himself around his boss's office in Fight Club.
sentences.zh: 就像《搏击俱乐部》里爱德华·诺顿在老板办公室里横冲直撞一样。

sentences.en: Like the kleptomaniac that Tippi Hedren played in Alfred Hitchcock's Marnie.
sentences.zh: 就像蒂比·海德莉在阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克的《艳贼》中扮演的那个盗窃癖患者。

sentences.en: Trying to palm a stack of cash, but her arm just won't pick it up.
sentences.zh: 试图抓起一叠现金，但她的手臂就是抬不起来。

sentences.en: At some point, I stopped straining.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，我不再强撑了。

sentences.en: This wasn't the struggle I came for.
sentences.zh: 这不是我所追求的斗争。

sentences.en: Plus, a friend told me later that I had made my fist wrong.
sentences.zh: 另外，后来有个朋友告诉我，我的拳头握错了。

sentences.en: The Black Power salute is not a casual gesture.
sentences.zh: “黑人权力”礼不是一个随意的动作。

sentences.en: It's weaponry.
sentences.zh: 它是武器。

sentences.en: You aim that arm and fire.
sentences.zh: 你要瞄准那条手臂，然后发射。

sentences.en: I aimed mine in solidarity.
sentences.zh: 我瞄准的是团结。

sentences.en: With white people, instead of at a system, they personify.
sentences.zh: 对着白人，而不是对着他们所代表的那个体制。

sentences.en: And that didn't feel quite right.
sentences.zh: 那感觉不太对劲。

sentences.en: But how would I know?
sentences.zh: 但我怎么会知道呢？

sentences.en: I had never done a Black Power salute.
sentences.zh: 我从未做过“黑人力量”的致敬手势。

sentences.en: It always seemed like more Blackness than I've needed.
sentences.zh: 那似乎比我所需要的黑人特质要多得多。

sentences.en: Maybe more than I had.
sentences.zh: 也许比我所拥有的还要多。

sentences.en: I'm not Black Power Black.
sentences.zh: 我不是那种“黑人力量”式的黑人。

sentences.en: I've always been milder, more apprehensive than that.
sentences.zh: 我一直以来都更温和，也更忧虑。

sentences.en: I was practically born with a mustache.
sentences.zh: 我几乎是留着胡子出生的。

sentences.en: I grew up in Philadelphia in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 我在20世纪80年代的费城长大。

sentences.en: My mother left my father when my sister and I was small.
sentences.zh: 在我妹妹和我还小的时候，我母亲就离开了父亲。

sentences.en: I took the divorce just fine, except for the stealing.
sentences.zh: 除了偷窃这件事，我处理离婚的方式还算不错。

sentences.en: I used to pluck quarters from my mother's change person before class, feed them to the arcade consoles at the 7-Eleven near school.
sentences.zh: 上课前，我常从母亲的零钱袋里偷硬币，塞进学校附近7-Eleven便利店的街机里。

sentences.en: First, though, I would discreetly jam handfuls of one-cent candy into my pockets.
sentences.zh: 不过，在那之前，我会不动声色地往口袋里塞一把把的一分钱糖果。

sentences.en: The quarters were never meant to cover that.
sentences.zh: 那些硬币从来都不是为了付这个钱。

sentences.en: For two weeks in the second grade, this is how my mornings began.
sentences.zh: 在二年级的两周里，我的早晨就是这样开始的。

sentences.en: Until I got caught.
sentences.zh: 直到我被抓住了。

sentences.en: The store manager called my mother, and in the uncomfortably long wait for her arrival, I sat there, wallowing in regret.
sentences.zh: 店经理给我母亲打了电话，在等待她到来的那段令人难熬的漫长时间里，我坐在那里，沉浸在懊悔之中。

sentences.en: But she never showed.
sentences.zh: 但她没来。

sentences.en: My father did.
sentences.zh: 是我父亲来的。

sentences.en: She must have phoned him.
sentences.zh: 她一定是给他打了电话。

sentences.en: He walked me home to the house he no longer lived in and spanked me.
sentences.zh: 他陪我走回他已经不住的那栋房子，并打了我的屁股。

sentences.en: A first for us both.
sentences.zh: 这对我们俩来说都是第一次。

sentences.en: Then he calmly walked me to school.
sentences.zh: 然后他平静地送我去了学校。

sentences.en: On the way, he explained, with uncharacteristic gravity, that because I was black, I needed to be very careful about my behavior.
sentences.zh: 路上，他以一种不同寻常的严肃态度向我解释说，因为我是黑人，所以我必须非常注意自己的言行。

sentences.en: Nobody should steal, and we especially shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 谁都不应该偷东西，而我们尤其不应该。

sentences.en: He was a track coach, and that was one of the few times he ever coached me.
sentences.zh: 他是一名田径教练，那也是他为数不多指导我的时候之一。

sentences.en: It's perhaps absurd to point to one childhood incident and declare it decisive, but I've always found that story useful.
sentences.zh: 指出童年的一件事并宣称它具有决定性意义或许很荒谬，但我一直觉得那个故事很有用。

sentences.en: It's rich in disappointment, embarrassment, shame, and guilt.
sentences.zh: 它充满了失望、尴尬、羞耻和内疚。

sentences.en: My mother needed those quarters.
sentences.zh: 我母亲需要那些硬币。

sentences.en: They were car fare, and the kids at school now knew I was a thief.
sentences.zh: 那是车费，而且学校里的孩子们现在都知道我是个小偷了。

sentences.en: I was so ashamed that I vowed at six that I never wanted to feel like that again.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常羞愧，以至于我在六岁时就发誓，我再也不想有那种感觉了。

sentences.en: I'd had a moral near-death experience.
sentences.zh: 我经历了一次道德上的濒死体验。

sentences.en: From there on, I would be good.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我要做一个好孩子。

sentences.en: That was the vow.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个誓言。

sentences.en: I would be good.
sentences.zh: 我要做一个好孩子。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night, you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，每天晚上，你都要带着你最珍视的300件宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你会把DJ台变成一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用一个月《时报》，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Good meant trying hard and helping out and listening and being a devoted friend.
sentences.zh: “好”意味着努力尝试、乐于助人、善于倾听并成为一个忠诚的朋友。

sentences.en: It meant only the best news for my parents and being liked.
sentences.zh: 这意味着只给父母带去最好的消息，并讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: But goodness as a personal policy is strange for a child to have.
sentences.zh: 但把“善良”作为一种个人准则对孩子来说很奇怪。

sentences.en: It's for grown-ups, not for kids.
sentences.zh: 那是大人的事，不是孩子的。

sentences.en: Teachers like good kids.
sentences.zh: 老师喜欢好孩子。

sentences.en: Some teachers prefer them.
sentences.zh: 有些老师更偏爱他们。

sentences.en: The kind of goodness I'm talking about is suspicious to other kids.
sentences.zh: 我所说的这种“好”在其他孩子看来是可疑的。

sentences.en: Kids don't want to catch you abstaining from trouble or raising your hand or staying behind after school to help out or, worse, to hang.
sentences.zh: 孩子们不喜欢看到你远离麻烦、积极举手、放学后留下来帮忙，或者更糟的是，留下来闲逛。

sentences.en: I went to the same small, mostly black private school from third grade until graduation.
sentences.zh: 从三年级到毕业，我一直就读于同一所小型、以黑人为主的私立学校。

sentences.en: That kind of goodness sometimes got classified as white.
sentences.zh: 那种“好”有时会被归类为“白人式”。

sentences.en: It wasn't pejorative, exactly.
sentences.zh: 那倒不完全是贬义。

sentences.en: Kids liked me.
sentences.zh: 孩子们喜欢我。

sentences.en: But we all seemed to realize that now I had a genre.
sentences.zh: 但我们似乎都意识到，现在的我被贴上了一个标签。

sentences.en: I don't recall making a conscious equation between goodness and whiteness.
sentences.zh: 我不记得自己曾有意识地将“善良”与“白人特质”划等号。

sentences.en: But I watched TV and went to movies and devoured comic books and music videos in which most of the people were white.
sentences.zh: 但我看电视、看电影，沉迷于漫画书和音乐录影带，里面大多数人都是白人。

sentences.en: I made identifications.
sentences.zh: 我产生了认同感。

sentences.en: I internalized things.
sentences.zh: 我内化了一些东西。

sentences.en: I watched almost every episode of two popular sitcoms in which rich white people adopt black orphans.
sentences.zh: 我几乎看完了两部热门情景喜剧的每一集，剧里都是富有的白人收养了黑人孤儿。

sentences.en: Hip-hop had only begun its pursuit of world domination.
sentences.zh: 嘻哈音乐当时才刚刚开始追求统治世界。

sentences.en: It was still just rap.
sentences.zh: 那还仅仅是说唱。

sentences.en: But I preferred pop music and liked it when a rap song
sentences.zh: 但我更喜欢流行音乐，并且喜欢当一首说唱歌曲——

sentences.en: Push It, Just a Friend, Going Back to Cali crossed from black radio to everybody else's.
sentences.zh: 比如《Push It》、《Just a Friend》、《Going Back to Cali》——从黑人电台跨界到大众电台时。

sentences.en: The crossing over was validating.
sentences.zh: 这种跨界是一种认可。

sentences.en: Pop was proof not of selling out, but of a kind of goodness.
sentences.zh: 流行并非背叛，而是一种善良的证明。

sentences.en: I never suffered any major drama about being black or being gay.
sentences.zh: 关于身为黑人或身为同性恋，我从未经历过什么重大的戏剧性事件。

sentences.en: A stretch of the sixth grade featured me talking like Jack A.
sentences.zh: 六年级有一段时间，我说话像杰克·A。

sentences.en: Harry, who played the flamboyantly congested sex spot, Sandra, on 227.
sentences.zh: 哈里，他在《227》中饰演那个风骚又做作的性感角色桑德拉。

sentences.en: I just understood that there were strata, and somewhere among them were my proper diction and pegged genes.
sentences.zh: 我只是明白社会存在阶层，而在这些阶层中，有我那得体的措辞和卷起的裤脚。

sentences.en: I had made myself an individual and was never tortured too terribly for it.
sentences.zh: 我把自己塑造成了一个独立的个体，从未因此受到过太严重的折磨。

sentences.en: I had a little room of my own in a wider black world.
sentences.zh: 在更广阔的黑人世界里，我有自己的一小片天地。

sentences.en: Then Carlton moved in.
sentences.zh: 然后卡尔顿搬进来了。

sentences.en: Carlton was Will Smith's rich, conservative cousin on The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿是威尔·史密斯在《新鲜王子妙事多》中那个富有、保守的表弟。

sentences.en: The show ran on NBC from 1990 to 1996 and was another black adoption sitcom.
sentences.zh: 该剧于1990年至1996年在NBC播出，是另一部关于黑人收养的情景喜剧。

sentences.en: Only the rich family was black.
sentences.zh: 只是这次富有的家庭是黑人。

sentences.en: Carlton was the middle kid, bellowingly enunciative, preppy in Ralph Lauren everything, deafened by the setting on Will's blackness.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿是中间的孩子，说话声音洪亮，从头到脚都是拉尔夫·劳伦的预科生风格，对威尔的黑人特质设置充耳不闻。

sentences.en: To Will, Carlton's familiarity with whiteness made him indistinguishable from it.
sentences.zh: 对威尔来说，卡尔顿对白人文化的熟悉让他与白人无异。

sentences.en: Early in season one, when a family friend chooses Carlton and not Will to drive his fancy car to Palm Springs as a favor, a miffed Will asks,
sentences.zh: 第一季初期，当一位家庭朋友选择卡尔顿而不是威尔，让他帮忙开车送自己去棕榈泉时，恼火的威尔问道：

sentences.en: This is a black thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是黑人特有的事，对吧？

sentences.en: On the road, Carlton offers Will a snack.
sentences.zh: 在路上，卡尔顿给威尔提供零食。

sentences.en: What do you say to an Oreo?
sentences.zh: 你对奥利奥（Oreo）怎么看？

sentences.en: Will answers,
sentences.zh: 威尔回答道：

sentences.en: What's up, Carlton?
sentences.zh: 怎么了，卡尔顿？

sentences.en: Carlton's erudition and country club style panic Will, whose own approach to blackness becomes an overcompensation for his proximity to affluence.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿的博学和乡村俱乐部风格让威尔感到恐慌，威尔自己对黑人身份的处理方式，成了他因接近富裕阶层而产生的过度补偿。

sentences.en: His blackness is a thing he performs, for an audience, but mainly for himself.
sentences.zh: 他的黑人身份是他表演给观众看的东西，但主要是表演给自己看的。

sentences.en: In season two, Uncle Phil tells Will that he's proud of him, that he's just like his son.
sentences.zh: 在第二季中，菲尔叔叔告诉威尔他为他感到骄傲，说他就像自己的儿子一样。

sentences.en: It's a compliment that induces a nervous breakdown.
sentences.zh: 这是一个引发他精神崩溃的赞美。

sentences.en: I'm turning into Carlton, Will says.
sentences.zh: “我正在变成卡尔顿，”威尔说。

sentences.en: No more of these sissy sandwiches, no more valet parking, and no more of these preppy parties, man.
sentences.zh: “别再吃这些娘娘腔的三明治了，别再代客泊车了，也别再参加这些预科生的派对了，伙计。”

sentences.en: He then destroys the $200 check that he kissed up to Uncle Phil to write him, and says,
sentences.zh: 然后他撕毁了那张他为了讨好菲尔叔叔才让他开的200美元支票，并说道：

sentences.en: Yo, the funky fresh is back in the flesh with a vengeance, Holmes.
sentences.zh: “哟，那个时髦又新鲜的家伙带着复仇回来了，福尔摩斯。”

sentences.en: It's stunning enough, the equation of intelligence with emasculation and whiteness with lunch,
sentences.zh: 将智慧等同于阉割，将白人特质等同于午餐，这已经够令人震惊了，

sentences.en: Will, sandwiches?
sentences.zh: “威尔，三明治？”

sentences.en: But when he's finished, the audience erupts in cheers.
sentences.zh: 但当他说完时，观众爆发出欢呼声。

sentences.en: Nobody watching wanted Will to become good.
sentences.zh: 没有观众希望威尔变好。

sentences.en: They wanted him to stay black.
sentences.zh: 他们希望他保持黑人的样子。

sentences.en: I didn't know who Carlton was until I was presumed to be him.
sentences.zh: 在被人认定是卡尔顿之前，我根本不知道他是谁。

sentences.en: In school, at my weekend movie theater job, in the checkout line at The Gap,
sentences.zh: 在学校里，在我周末的电影院工作中，在Gap的结账队伍里，

sentences.en: he equipped the young and perplexed with a shorthand for bright, square oddballs who weren't quite nerds.
sentences.zh: 他为那些年轻而困惑的人提供了一个简写，用来形容那些聪明、刻板、古怪，但又不算书呆子的人。

sentences.en: Nerds were easy.
sentences.zh: 书呆子很好辨认。

sentences.en: They were Steve Urkel, the geek from Family Matters.
sentences.zh: 他们是史蒂夫·厄克尔，《凡人琐事》里的那个极客。

sentences.en: In high school, there were a few of us oddballs.
sentences.zh: 在高中，我们这些怪人有几个。

sentences.en: I, alas, was the lone Carlton.
sentences.zh: 唉，我是唯一的卡尔顿。

sentences.en: But a crucial part of the equation always felt off.
sentences.zh: 但这个等式中关键的一部分总觉得不对劲。

sentences.en: Carlton epitomized the hazardous comedy of racial estrangement.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿是种族疏离这种危险喜剧的缩影。

sentences.en: Even his assertions of blackness were meant in irony.
sentences.zh: 即使是他对黑人身份的宣称也是带有讽刺意味的。

sentences.en: Like the time in season one when Will bets that his cousin wouldn't last long in Compton and Carlton winds up dressed like a gangster.
sentences.zh: 就像第一季里威尔打赌说他表弟在康普顿待不久，结果卡尔顿打扮得像个黑帮成员一样。

sentences.en: His sudden abundance of blackness was supposedly funnier because we were well-versed in his alleged lack of it.
sentences.zh: 他突然表现出的丰富黑人特质被认为更好笑，因为我们都很清楚他所谓的“缺乏”黑人特质。

sentences.en: But sometimes I wondered, was he really an exemplar of blackness's rigidity, or could he have been an exploration of its parameters?
sentences.zh: 但有时我怀疑，他真的是黑人身份僵化的典范，还是说他其实是对其参数的一种探索？

sentences.en: Could I?
sentences.zh: 我呢？

sentences.en: I don't think it mattered back then.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当时这并不重要。

sentences.en: These were teenagers.
sentences.zh: 他们只是青少年。

sentences.en: They weren't looking for the nuances of who anybody was.
sentences.zh: 他们并不关心某人到底是什么样的人。

sentences.en: They were Will in search of the easiest path to jokes that distracted from their insecurities.
sentences.zh: 他们就像威尔一样，在寻找最简单的笑话路径，以掩盖他们的不安全感。

sentences.en: And the path from Carlton to me was, admittedly, not an arduous one to forge.
sentences.zh: 而从卡尔顿到我这条路，不得不承认，并不难走。

sentences.en: This would have been asking a lot of a network sitcom.
sentences.zh: 这对于一部电视情景喜剧来说要求太高了。

sentences.en: But I sometimes wondered about the blackness of Carlton's inner life and its correspondence to mine.
sentences.zh: 但我有时会思考卡尔顿内心世界的黑人特质，以及它与我的对应关系。

sentences.en: One of the proudest secondhand moments of my adolescence was the Wimbledon tennis tournament in which an unseated Laurie McNeil stopped Steffi Graf's title defense in the first round and almost made it to the final.
sentences.zh: 我青春期最引以为傲的间接时刻之一是温布尔登网球锦标赛，当时未被列为种子的劳里·麦克尼尔在第一轮就终结了施特菲·格拉芙的卫冕之路，并差点打进决赛。

sentences.en: I liked Steffi Graf, but Laurie McNeil?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢施特菲·格拉芙，但劳里·麦克尼尔？

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Did Carlton catch any of that?
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿注意到了吗？

sentences.en: Did he love it when a curmudgeon like Stanley Crouch, a reality checker like Julianne Malveaux,
sentences.zh: 当像斯坦利·克劳奇这样的老顽固，像朱莉安·马尔沃这样的现实核查者，

sentences.en: or a sage like Toni Morrison would show up on some talk show and just go on and on about whatever?
sentences.zh: 或者像托妮·莫里森这样的智者出现在脱口秀节目上，滔滔不绝地谈论各种话题时，他会喜欢吗？

sentences.en: The hosts might have seemed prepared for the erudite truth of what they had to say, but often seemed taken aback by the precise blackness of its deployment.
sentences.zh: 主持人可能对他们所说内容的博学真相有所准备，但往往会被其展现出的精确黑人特质所震惊。

sentences.en: The joke of Carlton was that he adored Tom Jones and danced like Belinda Carlisle,
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿的笑点在于他崇拜汤姆·琼斯，跳舞像贝琳达·卡莱尔，

sentences.en: but surely he could sense that the 1980s and 1990s were a bounteous age for an anything-goes kind of blackness.
sentences.zh: 但他肯定能感觉到20世纪80年代和90年代是一个黑人特质百花齐放的时代。

sentences.en: Prince, Whoopi Goldberg, Jermaine Stewart, Janet Jackson, Flavor Flav.
sentences.zh: 王子、乌比·戈德堡、杰梅因·斯图尔特、珍妮特·杰克逊、弗拉瓦·弗拉夫。

sentences.en: The first time I saw a wetsuit was on Corey Glover, who sang in the band Living Color.
sentences.zh: 我第一次看到潜水服是在科里·格洛弗身上，他在Living Color乐队唱歌。

sentences.en: Four black guys who built their hard rock on a bass layer of rhythm and blues.
sentences.zh: 四个黑人小伙子，他们以节奏蓝调为低音基础，构建了自己的硬摇滚。

sentences.en: Rapsmen you had diversified enough to include Afrocentric hippies like Arrested Development and hippie dorks like De La Soul.
sentences.zh: 说唱歌手们已经多元化到包括像Arrested Development这样的非洲中心主义嬉皮士，以及像De La Soul这样的嬉皮书呆子。

sentences.en: Lenny Kravitz was another hippie, but nobody in my life seemed to take his funk rock as spiritually as I did.
sentences.zh: 兰尼·克拉维茨是另一个嬉皮士，但生活中似乎没人像我那样从精神层面理解他的放克摇滚。

sentences.en: To them, it was cheesy and ripped off.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，那很俗气，而且是抄袭。

sentences.en: I inspected this music for a blackness that comported with mine and every time felt the thrill of pure identification.
sentences.zh: 我审视这些音乐，寻找与我相符的黑人特质，每次都能感受到纯粹认同的快感。

sentences.en: Carlton rarely got to make any such discovery.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿很少能有这样的发现。

sentences.en: His cluelessness was too useful an asset.
sentences.zh: 他的无知是一个太有用的资产了。

sentences.en: He was the bane of my adolescence, but I came to feel for him and despise the trap he was in.
sentences.zh: 他是我的青春期克星，但我开始同情他，并鄙视他所处的陷阱。

sentences.en: Every once in a while, though, somebody involved with that show would let him be the littlest bit loose.
sentences.zh: 不过，偶尔也会有人让那个角色稍微放松一点。

sentences.en: At the end of the Compton episode, this happens.
sentences.zh: 在康普顿那一集的结尾，发生了这一幕。

sentences.en: Carlton, I never judge you for being the way you are, but you always act like I don't measure up to some rule of blackness that you carry around.
sentences.zh: “威尔，我从不评判你的为人，但你总是表现得好像我达不到你随身携带的某种黑人标准一样。”

sentences.en: Will, you treat me like I'm some kind of idiot just because I talk different.
sentences.zh: “威尔，你总是把我当成某种白痴，仅仅因为我说话方式不同。”

sentences.en: Carlton, differently.
sentences.zh: “卡尔顿，是‘不同地’（differently）。”

sentences.en: The show just kept shaking the Etch-A-Sketch, resetting Carlton's self-awareness and Will's insensitivity to it.
sentences.zh: 这部剧只是不断地摇晃着画板，重置了卡尔顿的自我意识和威尔对它的迟钝。

sentences.en: But I understood what Will's ilk ignored.
sentences.zh: 但我理解威尔这类人所忽视的东西。

sentences.en: The Oreo had a soul.
sentences.zh: 奥利奥也是有灵魂的。

sentences.en: During that stretch in high school, I grew a mustache.
sentences.zh: 高中那段时间，我留起了胡子。

sentences.en: It was a classic rite of male puberty.
sentences.zh: 这是男性青春期的一种经典仪式。

sentences.en: I grew it because I could.
sentences.zh: 我留胡子是因为我能留。

sentences.en: Kept it because it didn't violate a dress code and was grateful for it because it probably helped tame the homophobes.
sentences.zh: 我留着它是因为它没违反着装规定，而且我很感激它，因为它可能帮我震慑住了那些恐同者。

sentences.en: Just about every boy in my graduating class had something sprouting above their lip.
sentences.zh: 我那一届的男生几乎每个人嘴唇上方都冒出了一些东西。

sentences.en: Wispy, ghostly, cheesy, but certifiably masculine.
sentences.zh: 稀疏、虚幻、滑稽，但确实是男性的象征。

sentences.en: That's also why people called me Carlton, because I bore the vaguest resemblance to Alfonso Ribeiro, the actor who played him.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么人们叫我卡尔顿，因为我长得和饰演他的演员阿方索·里贝罗有几分神似。

sentences.en: We both talked funny, dressed funny, danced funny, and we both, it must be said, had a mustache.
sentences.zh: 我们说话、穿衣、跳舞的风格都很滑稽，而且必须得说，我们都留着胡子。

sentences.en: On my way to college, I got rid of it, hoping to exercise Carlton.
sentences.zh: 上大学前，我把它刮了，希望能摆脱卡尔顿的影子。

sentences.en: And it didn't go with the look I wanted to take with me.
sentences.zh: 而且它和我想要展现的形象也不搭。

sentences.en: Baggy T-shirts and baggy pants with either Doc Martens or a pair of Chuck Taylors.
sentences.zh: 宽大的T恤和裤子，再配上马汀博士靴或匡威帆布鞋。

sentences.en: I had two beloved T-shirts.
sentences.zh: 我有两件心爱的T恤。

sentences.en: Travis Bickle, the taxi driver Psycho, was printed on one.
sentences.zh: 一件印着《出租车司机》里那个精神病患者特拉维斯·比克尔。

sentences.en: One, the other, was striped thin in red, green, black, and yellow, which struck me as in some way African, even though it was not.
sentences.zh: 另一件有红、绿、黑、黄的细条纹，这让我觉得它带点非洲风情，尽管事实并非如此。

sentences.en: My older cousin Leon bought me a 40 acres and a mule baseball cap from Spike Lee's merchandise shop.
sentences.zh: 我堂哥莱昂从斯派克·李的周边店给我买了一顶印有“40英亩和一头骡子”的棒球帽。

sentences.en: No filmmaker mattered more to my teenage self, but I was perpetually concerned that somebody might ask what the 40 acres were all about.
sentences.zh: 对我青少年时期而言，没有哪位电影制作人比他更重要，但我总是担心有人会问那“40英亩”到底是什么意思。

sentences.en: Here I was, nervous about the call for reparations atop my head when there was a homicidal maniac staring out from my cheSt.
sentences.zh: 当时的我，头顶着关于赔偿的诉求感到不安，而胸前却印着一个杀人狂的头像。

sentences.en: Even then, I couldn't make a fiSt.
sentences.zh: 即便在那时，我也无法握紧拳头。

sentences.en: I went to Yale, which, until recently, offered an orientation camp for several dozen non-white students to bond.
sentences.zh: 我去了耶鲁大学，直到最近，该校还为几十名非白人学生提供迎新营，让他们建立联系。

sentences.en: It was a week of sitting around, exploiting the pretext of food and talent shows to luxuriate in the personalities and tastes and lives of potential new friends.
sentences.zh: 那是一周的时间，大家聚在一起，借着美食和才艺表演的幌子，尽情享受着潜在新朋友的个性、品味和生活。

sentences.en: It was exciting finding these kindred souls.
sentences.zh: 能找到这些志同道合的灵魂真是令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Every once in a while, one of us would pause our little paradise to laugh at the absurdity of it all.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，我们中的某个人会暂停这小小的天堂，嘲笑这一切的荒谬。

sentences.en: Well, the program's acronym was PROP, and ponder the looming menace.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个项目的缩写是PROP，想想那迫在眉睫的威胁吧。

sentences.en: Were we being warned?
sentences.zh: 我们是在被警告吗？

sentences.en: The program was a rather stunning admission on the college's part.
sentences.zh: 这个项目是校方一个相当惊人的承认。

sentences.en: This is a white place.
sentences.zh: 这是一个白人的地盘。

sentences.en: You all are going to need to keep one another from drowning.
sentences.zh: 你们所有人得互相扶持，免得被淹没。

sentences.en: Lots of us had gone to integrated schools.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人都上过种族融合的学校。

sentences.en: We could swim.
sentences.zh: 我们会游泳。

sentences.en: I swam.
sentences.zh: 我游过。

sentences.en: But there's a way that, for certain non-white people, especially if you're poor, life at a liberal arts college, especially a so-called elite one,
sentences.zh: 但对于某些非白人来说，尤其是如果你很贫穷，在文理学院，特别是在所谓的精英学校里，生活方式有一种感觉，

sentences.en: can feel like the reward for all of that being good.
sentences.zh: 就像是你表现良好的回报。

sentences.en: Maybe you've beaten some odds to get there, and your prize for all of the effort, and, let's face it,
sentences.zh: 也许你克服了一些困难才来到这里，而你所有努力的奖赏，说实话，

sentences.en: all of the luck, is, yes, a premium education, but also living among white people.
sentences.zh: 还有所有的运气，确实是一份优质的教育，但同时也意味着生活在白人中间。

sentences.en: But first, ha-ha, first, you must exemplify your people, be a diplomat for them, and an ambassador to the white people to whom your ways might seem foreign.
sentences.zh: 但首先，哈哈，首先，你必须成为你族群的典范，做他们的外交官，做那些对你的方式感到陌生的白人的大使。

sentences.en: No one ever puts it that way.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人会这么说。

sentences.en: The structure does the talking.
sentences.zh: 这种结构本身就在说话。

sentences.en: No black first-year student I knew at Yale had a black roommate.
sentences.zh: 我在耶鲁认识的黑人新生里，没有一个有黑人室友。

sentences.en: If a professor put James Baldwin or Tony Morrison or Ntozaki Shange or August Wilson on a syllabus,
sentences.zh: 如果教授在课程大纲里列出了詹姆斯·鲍德温、托妮·莫里森、恩托扎克·尚格或奥古斯特·威尔逊的作品，

sentences.en: you, as the section's sole black person, would be gazed at until you got the discussion started, expected to approve your section mate's analysis and withstand their insinuations.
sentences.zh: 作为小组里唯一的黑人，你会一直被盯着看，直到你开启讨论，大家期待你认可小组同伴的分析，并承受他们的暗示。

sentences.en: There were several ways to receive such a position.
sentences.zh: 面对这种处境有几种方式。

sentences.en: AghaSt.
sentences.zh: 震惊。

sentences.en: Aggrieved.
sentences.zh: 委屈。

sentences.en: In acquiescence.
sentences.zh: 默许。

sentences.en: With authority.
sentences.zh: 权威。

sentences.en: I eventually owned the situation, but it created delusions.
sentences.zh: 我最终掌控了局面，但这产生了错觉。

sentences.en: I, at least, went through a brief, shameful period of high peacock, during which my stage name could have been Mr. Black Experience.
sentences.zh: 至少，我经历了一段短暂而羞耻的“孔雀期”，在那期间，我的艺名本可以叫“黑人体验先生”。

sentences.en: Prolonged onlyness winds up abutting exceptionalism.
sentences.zh: 长期的孤独最终会演变成精英主义。

sentences.en: The alternatives never felt, to me, like improvements.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，其他的选择从来都不觉得是改善。

sentences.en: Take the athlete from Southern California whom I ran into during a terrible evening he was having our first year.
sentences.zh: 就拿我大一那年在一个糟糕的夜晚遇到的那个南加州运动员来说吧。

sentences.en: The pressure to declare his blackness had snapped him.
sentences.zh: 宣示黑人身份的压力让他崩溃了。

sentences.en: He didn't want to merely be some black guy.
sentences.zh: 他不想仅仅成为某个“黑人哥们”。

sentences.en: He just wanted to be him.
sentences.zh: 他只想做他自己。

sentences.en: There was no consolation.
sentences.zh: 没有任何安慰。

sentences.en: We ran into each other from time to time.
sentences.zh: 我们不时会碰到。

sentences.en: He pledged one of the big white fraternities and seemed to enjoy its spoils.
sentences.zh: 他加入了白人兄弟会，似乎很享受其中的好处。

sentences.en: I still think about him.
sentences.zh: 我至今还会想起他。

sentences.en: What were the rest of his four years like?
sentences.zh: 他剩下的四年是怎么过的？

sentences.en: Mine remained four of my beSt.
sentences.zh: 而我剩下的四年是我最好的时光。

sentences.en: I was happy.
sentences.zh: 我很开心。

sentences.en: Only this summer have I taken any deep stock of the time I had there.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，我才对自己在那里的时光进行了深刻的盘点。

sentences.en: How acculturation can breed estrangement.
sentences.zh: 文化适应是如何滋生疏离感的。

sentences.en: How I ended up with a comfortable life I've got.
sentences.zh: 我是如何过上现在这种舒适生活的。

sentences.en: One urgent demand of this moment is for people, workplaces, and institutions to reckon with their whiteness.
sentences.zh: 当下的一项紧迫要求是，人们、工作场所和机构必须正视他们的白人属性。

sentences.en: Why not reckon with mine?
sentences.zh: 为什么不正视我的呢？

sentences.en: Day after day of video calls will do that.
sentences.zh: 日复一日的视频通话就会让你这么做。

sentences.en: I sat there on work meetings and friend hangouts and family catch-ups and stared into people's homes, tallying who's in my world.
sentences.zh: 我坐在那里参加工作会议、朋友聚会和家庭联络，盯着人们的家，盘点着谁在我的世界里。

sentences.en: Regretting nothing but simply absorbing how solidly white and discreetly non-white the parties are and how it all feels traceable to a morning I got caught stuffing my pockets with Jolly Ranchers.
sentences.zh: 没什么好后悔的，只是单纯地吸收着这些聚会是多么纯粹的白人化，又是多么隐晦地非白人化，这一切似乎都可以追溯到我被抓到往口袋里塞糖果的那个早晨。

sentences.en: After graduation, during the decade and a half I spent working at newspapers in San Francisco and Boston, I embarked on a life that featured increasingly fewer black people.
sentences.zh: 毕业后，在旧金山和波士顿报社工作的十五年里，我开启了一种黑人越来越少的生活。

sentences.en: At the office, in restaurants, on the streets.
sentences.zh: 在办公室，在餐馆，在街上。

sentences.en: It was less an ambition than ambition's consequence.
sentences.zh: 这与其说是野心，不如说是野心的后果。

sentences.en: Some days, it felt as if the rapture had occurred and taken all the black people to Atlanta or Houston.
sentences.zh: 有时，感觉就像是“被提携”发生了，把所有的黑人都带到了亚特兰大或休斯顿。

sentences.en: Even as I basked in the fortune of my life, loneliness performed its gentle tin-tin-nabulations.
sentences.zh: 即使我沉浸在生活的幸运中，孤独感也在轻柔地敲响警钟。

sentences.en: San Francisco once had a good, black-run soul food place called Powell's.
sentences.zh: 旧金山曾经有一家不错的黑人经营的灵魂乐餐厅，叫鲍威尔餐厅。

sentences.en: I sat down there almost every month just to have a base to touch.
sentences.zh: 我几乎每个月都会去那里坐坐，只是为了找个落脚点。

sentences.en: I talked about moving to Oakland, but never did.
sentences.zh: 我谈过搬到奥克兰，但从未付诸行动。

sentences.en: In Boston, I had a couple of weird years with men.
sentences.zh: 在波士顿，我和男人们有过几年奇怪的经历。

sentences.en: After a political convention in 2004, I took home a guy from South Carolina who seduced me with talk about the difference he planned to make as a black politician.
sentences.zh: 2004年一次政治大会后，我带回了一个南卡罗来纳州的男人，他用他计划作为黑人政治家所能带来的改变的话语诱惑了我。

sentences.en: On the walk to the subway the next morning, I all but asked him to take me to Charleston.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上走去地铁站的路上，我差点就让他带我去查尔斯顿了。

sentences.en: That was the end of that.
sentences.zh: 那段关系就此结束。

sentences.en: I wasn't thinking of the people in my life as just white people.
sentences.zh: 我并没有把生活中的人仅仅看作是白人。

sentences.en: These were my co-workers, my friends.
sentences.zh: 他们是我的同事，我的朋友。

sentences.en: One of those friends applied a similar logic to me.
sentences.zh: 其中一个朋友对我应用了类似的逻辑。

sentences.en: The same week that a Minneapolis police officer killed Philando Castile, he found me in grief.
sentences.zh: 就在明尼阿波利斯警察杀害菲兰多·卡斯蒂尔的那一周，他发现我在悲伤。

sentences.en: And I told him that I've always harbored a murmuring awareness that I could be shot.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他，我一直有一种隐约的意识，觉得自己也可能会被枪杀。

sentences.en: He was incredulous.
sentences.zh: 他表示怀疑。

sentences.en: How could that happen to me?
sentences.zh: 这种事怎么可能发生在我身上？

sentences.en: I went to a good school and had a good job.
sentences.zh: 我上了好学校，有一份好工作。

sentences.en: I was black, but not killed during a police stop black.
sentences.zh: 我是黑人，但不是那种会在警察拦截时被杀的黑人。

sentences.en: I was good.
sentences.zh: 我是个“好人”。

sentences.en: I can imagine a version of myself that, having completed Yale and succeeded professionally, would have heard that response and felt relieved.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象出另一个版本的自己，在耶鲁毕业并事业有成后，听到那样的回应会感到宽慰。

sentences.en: That I was one of racism's carve-outs.

sentences.en: I can now see that my vow of goodness was an existential shift of shape.

sentences.en: Having been told early on that unreasonable obstacles awaited, I set about finding a form that could easily evade them.

sentences.en: There is, I suppose, another hand, wherein I take further stock and declare a folly.

sentences.en: The entire affair of race is a joke.

sentences.en: In the United States, a black self eventually discovers his race is a form of credit, or discredit, as it were.

sentences.en: You can't leave home without it.

sentences.en: Yet for as long as black Americans have been conscious of their blackness, some public intellectual has cried, hoax.
sentences.zh: 然而，只要美国黑人意识到自己的黑人身份，就会有公共知识分子大喊：骗局。

sentences.en: You, black person, are free.

sentences.en: Lately, and most cantankerously, it's Kanye West who has been daring to level with us.

sentences.en: His vision for transcendence of racism, if not race itself, would be easier to share if it didn't appear to lead straight into the arms of racists.
sentences.zh: 如果他的愿景不是直接导致投向种族主义者的怀抱，那么他关于超越种族主义（如果不是超越种族本身）的愿景会更容易让人接受。

sentences.en: I don't believe in that kind of transcendence.

sentences.en: and feast on his decades-long search for a black self that suits him.

sentences.en: It's a finding book, a story of becoming.
sentences.zh: 这是一本寻找之书，一个关于“成为”的故事。

sentences.en: As the black tent expands, the people beneath it can keep doing as they've always done, widening its poles.

sentences.en: I have wondered, though, what kind of spiral I would have taken had the friend on that video call not said NAACP lawyer, if she had looked at my face and said,

sentences.en: The extant number of black firsts, rares, onlys, nevers, not yets, and not quites, attests to that, as does the chronic too-manyes, too-oftens, and too-soons.
sentences.zh: 现存的黑人“第一”、“稀有”、“唯一”、“从未”、“尚未”和“还不够”的数量证明了这一点，长期的“太多”、“太频繁”和“太早”也是如此。

sentences.en: I like to think that I would have absorbed her, Clarence Thomas, and regaled her with a separate lineage.

sentences.en: How did she kiss that thing and not need stitches?

sentences.en: My mother liked my stepfather's because, well, she loved him.
sentences.zh: 我母亲喜欢我继父的胡子，因为，嗯，她爱他。

sentences.en: My father had his phases.
sentences.zh: 我父亲的胡子则经历过不同阶段。

sentences.en: The fourth, Uncle Bill, had an ascot.

sentences.zh: 说谁没留过胡子，可能比说谁留过胡子要简单得多。

sentences.zh: 我不知道大家的政治立场如何，但作为一个家族，我们就像感恩节的餐桌一样丰富多样。

sentences.en: Their mustaches strike me now as a generational phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 如今看来，他们的胡子像是一种时代现象。

sentences.en: These people were all born between 1920 and 1950.
sentences.zh: 这些人都是出生于1920年到1950年之间。

sentences.en: Of their children, only my cousins, Butchie and Kyle, are describable as mustache men.
sentences.zh: 在他们的孩子中，只有我的表兄弟巴奇和凯尔，称得上是“胡子男”。

sentences.en: This is why I've kept mine.
sentences.zh: 这就是我留胡子的原因。

sentences.en: It's me squeezing my way into a parallel heritage.
sentences.zh: 这是我挤进一种平行传承的方式。

sentences.en: In this small sense, the work I do caring for it feels connected to a legacy of people who did and do the work chipping at and thinking with this nation.
sentences.zh: 从这个小小的意义上说，我打理胡子的工作，让我感觉与那些曾经并正在为这个国家添砖加瓦、思考未来的人们建立了一种联系。

sentences.en: Something obvious in just about any photograph taken of Black Americans during the Civil Rights era is how put together everyone is.
sentences.zh: 在民权运动时期拍摄的几乎每一张美国黑人照片中，显而易见的一点是，每个人都打扮得体。

sentences.zh: 他们去参加抗争时的着装，和去教堂时一样讲究。

sentences.en: The country was watching.
sentences.zh: 全国都在注视着。

sentences.en: People got dressed up to withstand being put down.
sentences.zh: 人们盛装打扮，以抵御受到的贬低。

sentences.en: They dressed with full awareness that an outfit risked ruin.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着时完全意识到，这身行头随时可能被毁掉。
